name: Elon Musk
bio_blurb: World's wealthiest person. Founded or co-founded Tesla, SpaceX, and Neuralink. Has given approximately 0.04% of his peak net worth to charity.

name: Jeff Bezos
bio_blurb: Founder of Amazon and Blue Origin. Pledged $10 billion to the Bezos Earth Fund in 2020 — a 10-year pledge representing less than 6% of his net worth at the time.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
bio_blurb: CEO of Meta. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative is structured as an LLC — not a foundation — meaning no mandatory payout, no IRS transparency, and Zuckerberg retains full control. His $45B pledge is in Meta stock over his lifetime.

name: Larry Ellison
bio_blurb: Co-founder of Oracle and the world's 4th wealthiest person. Despite signing the Giving Pledge in 2010, has given a tiny fraction of his wealth. Spends billions on personal real estate, including buying 98% of Lanai, Hawaii.

name: Warren Buffett
bio_blurb: CEO of Berkshire Hathaway. Has pledged to give away 99% of his wealth and donated over $50B to date — primarily to the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and his children's foundations. Among the most genuinely generous billionaires.

name: Bill Gates
bio_blurb: Co-founder of Microsoft. Has given away over $59B through the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, focused on global health, poverty, and US education. One of history's most significant philanthropists — though the foundation's ties to pharmaceutical interests raise questions about agenda-setting.

name: Michael Bloomberg
bio_blurb: Founder of Bloomberg LP and former NYC Mayor. Bloomberg Philanthropies has given over $14B with a focus on public health, climate, and arts. One of the more genuinely active philanthropists in the top 10.

name: Larry Page
bio_blurb: Co-founder of Google. Despite his massive wealth, Page has been notably absent from philanthropy. The Carl Victor Page Memorial Foundation gives sporadically and at levels far below peers. He has not signed the Giving Pledge.

name: Sergey Brin
bio_blurb: Google co-founder who signed the Giving Pledge in 2010. The Brin Wojcicki Foundation has given modestly relative to his net worth, primarily to medical research and disaster relief.

name: Steve Ballmer
bio_blurb: Former Microsoft CEO and owner of the LA Clippers. The Ballmer Group focuses on economic mobility for children and families in the US with a data-driven approach. Considered one of the more impact-focused major philanthropists.

name: Jim Walton
bio_blurb: Youngest son of Sam Walton. Runs Arvest Bank. Known for conservative philanthropy relative to his wealth. The Walton Family Foundation primarily funds charter schools — a philanthropic vehicle that critics argue undermines public education while serving family business interests.

name: Rob Walton
bio_blurb: Former Walmart chairman and eldest son of Sam Walton. Shares in the Walton Family Foundation with siblings. Relatively low profile philanthropically for someone of his wealth.

name: Alice Walton
bio_blurb: Walmart heiress and founder of Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art. Her philanthropy is primarily arts-focused in Bentonville, AR — building personal legacy infrastructure in a wealthy enclave rather than addressing systemic need.

name: Michael Dell
bio_blurb: Founder of Dell Technologies. The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation is considered one of the more impact-focused foundations among tech billionaires, concentrating on childhood poverty in US urban areas and global health.

name: Charles Koch
bio_blurb: CEO of Koch Industries. The Koch network of foundations and political organizations has donated billions — but primarily to libertarian/deregulatory advocacy that directly benefits Koch Industries' business interests. A significant portion goes to climate denial and anti-labor causes.

name: Ken Griffin
bio_blurb: Founder of Citadel hedge fund. Griffin has donated to museums and universities with naming rights attached. Also spent $300M+ on personal real estate and $700M on private art. Much of his philanthropy is legacy-building in elite institutions.

name: Stephen Schwarzman
bio_blurb: Co-founder of Blackstone. Has donated over $1B — largely to elite institutions like MIT, Yale, Oxford, and the NY Public Library with his name attached to each. Critics note that donations to elite universities primarily serve the ultra-wealthy and accelerate inequality.

name: Ray Dalio
bio_blurb: Founder of Bridgewater Associates. The Dalio Foundation focuses on ocean conservation and education. Primarily operates through DAFs and has received criticism for structuring giving to maximize tax advantages while maintaining control.

name: David Geffen
bio_blurb: Music and entertainment mogul. Major donor to UCLA (Geffen School of Medicine) and Lincoln Center — largely legacy-building in elite cultural institutions. Owns the world's largest privately-owned superyacht.

name: Phil Knight
bio_blurb: Nike co-founder. Has given significantly to University of Oregon and Stanford — both with his name attached. A significant portion of Knight's philanthropy funds elite universities and athletic facilities rather than addressing poverty or public health.

name: MacKenzie Scott
bio_blurb: Ex-wife of Jeff Bezos who has given away over $17B since 2019 in unrestricted grants to nonprofits — at a pace and scale unmatched by nearly any other billionaire. Uses a trust model with minimal overhead. A genuine outlier in billionaire philanthropy.

name: Rupert Murdoch
bio_blurb: Founder of News Corp and Fox Corporation. Has given minimally to charity relative to his net worth. His media empire has been accused of spreading misinformation that undermines public health and democratic institutions — negative social externalities not offset by limited giving.

name: John Mars
bio_blurb: Member of the Mars candy fortune family. Minimal documented philanthropy relative to his massive wealth. The Mars family is notable for privacy and for keeping wealth largely within the family.

name: Jacqueline Mars
bio_blurb: Granddaughter of Mars, Inc. founder. Has given to equestrian causes. Minimal documented philanthropy at the scale of her wealth.

name: Jensen Huang
bio_blurb: CEO of NVIDIA, whose net worth exploded during the AI boom. Has given modestly to Oregon State and Stanford. As one of the fastest-growing fortunes in history, his giving rate has not kept pace.

name: Len Blavatnik
bio_blurb: Ukrainian-born billionaire. Major donor to Harvard (Blavatnik School of Government at Oxford). Primarily gives to elite universities with naming rights attached.

name: Peter Thiel
bio_blurb: PayPal co-founder and venture capitalist. Has given primarily to libertarian political causes, anti-immigration campaigns, and life-extension research. Much of his 'philanthropy' serves his ideological agenda rather than broad social benefit.

name: John Paulson
bio_blurb: Hedge fund manager famous for shorting subprime mortgages in 2008. Gave $400M to Harvard in 2015 — the largest gift in Harvard's history at the time. Critics noted Harvard's $36B endowment hardly needed the funds compared to underfunded public institutions.

name: Marc Andreessen
bio_blurb: Co-founder of Netscape and a16z venture capital. Extremely vocal online, including publishing a 'Techno-Optimist Manifesto' opposing many forms of altruism and regulation. Documented charitable giving is negligible relative to his wealth.

name: Sam Altman
bio_blurb: CEO of OpenAI and former president of Y Combinator. Claims to work for humanity's benefit through AI. Documented personal charitable giving is minimal; most of his 'impact' is through OpenAI itself — a company in which he holds substantial equity.

name: Reed Hastings
bio_blurb: Netflix co-founder. Has given over $1B primarily to education — though largely to charter schools in a pattern aligned with business-minded education reform rather than fully public systems.

name: David Tepper
bio_blurb: Hedge fund manager and owner of the Carolina Panthers. Has given to Carnegie Mellon (Tepper School of Business) and other elite institutions. Giving is modest relative to his wealth.

name: Leon Black
bio_blurb: Co-founder of Apollo Global Management. Gave generously to Dartmouth and MoMA — but paid Jeffrey Epstein $158M for tax advice, later acknowledged as a serious lapse. Primarily legacy-building philanthropy.

name: Paul Singer
bio_blurb: Founder of Elliott Management, known as a 'vulture fund' that purchased Argentine and Puerto Rican debt at deep discounts and demanded full repayment, extracting billions from struggling sovereign nations. Philanthropically active but primarily in political and Israel-focused causes.

name: Jim Simons
bio_blurb: Founder of Renaissance Technologies. The Simons Foundation is one of the most substantial science philanthropies, investing over $5B in mathematics, basic science, and autism research. A genuinely impactful philanthropist.

name: Eric Schmidt
bio_blurb: Former Google CEO. The Schmidt Futures initiative funds science and technology education. Schmidt has been criticized for influence over AI policy through 'philanthropic' funding of government advisory bodies while simultaneously having financial interests in AI companies.

name: Andrew Forrest
bio_blurb: Australian billionaire and Giving Pledge signatory. One of the more impactful philanthropists among mining billionaires, with significant donations to climate, anti-trafficking, and indigenous causes through the Minderoo Foundation.

name: Patrick Collison
bio_blurb: Stripe CEO and co-founder. Has funded Fast Grants (rapid science funding during COVID), Arc Institute, and other high-impact giving vehicles. Considered one of the most thoughtful philanthropists in tech relative to his age and wealth.

name: Dustin Moskovitz
bio_blurb: Facebook co-founder who signed the Giving Pledge at 26. Funds Open Philanthropy, one of the most rigorous effective altruism-aligned foundations, focused on pandemic prevention, animal welfare, and AI safety. Among the most genuinely generous at his wealth level.

name: David Sacks
bio_blurb: PayPal co-founder and venture capitalist. Now serving in the Trump administration as AI Czar. Minimal documented charitable giving. Has used social media platform to promote political causes aligned with his investments.

name: Chamath Palihapitiya
bio_blurb: Former Facebook executive and SPAC king. Famous for saying he 'doesn't care' about Uyghur concentration camps. Social Capital focuses on technology investment, not philanthropy. Very limited documented charitable giving.

name: Jamie Dimon
bio_blurb: CEO of JPMorgan Chase, the largest US bank. Has overseen $30B in corporate 'racial equity commitments' — largely loans and investments, not genuine philanthropy. Personal giving is modest. JPMorgan paid $13B in settlements for its role in the 2008 financial crisis.

name: Ken Langone
bio_blurb: Home Depot co-founder and Wall Street financier. Has given significantly to NYU Langone Health — one of the largest hospital naming rights gifts. Critics note this primarily serves the wealthy enclave of NYU and Manhattan.

name: Oprah Winfrey
bio_blurb: Media mogul and philanthropist. Has given over $500M across education, poverty, and disaster relief. Among the most generous non-pledging billionaires relative to net worth. The Oprah Winfrey Foundation focuses on girls' education globally.
